**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 43, verses 15–19:**

**His saying, may He be exalted:** ﴿And they have assigned to Him a portion of His servants. Indeed, man is an evident ingrate.﴾ ﴿Has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen sons for you?﴾ ﴿And when one of them is given good tidings of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful, his face becomes dark and he suppresses grief.﴾ ﴿Is one who is brought up in ornaments, and who is unclear in disputation, [to be ascribed to Him]?﴾ ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, into females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded and they will be questioned.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, said ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [Luqman: 25], He showed that they, despite acknowledging this, have assigned to Him a portion of His servants. The purpose of this is to draw attention to the feebleness of their intellects and the foolishness of their minds. In the verse there are issues:

**The first issue:** ʿĀṣim, in the transmission of Abū Bakr, read *juzʾun* (جُزْءٌ) with a *ḍamma* on the *zāy* and the *hamza* throughout the Qur'an. Both are dialectal variants. As for Ḥamzah, when he pauses on it he says *juzan* (جُزًا) with a *fatḥa* on the *zāy* and without a *hamza*.

**The second issue:** Regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿and they have assigned to Him a portion of His servants﴾, there are two opinions:

The first, which is the well-known one, is that the intended meaning is that they attributed a child to Him. The sense of the statement is that a man's child is a part of him. He, peace be upon him, said: "Fatimah is a part of me" (ﷺ). Also, what is understood of a parent is that a part of his parts separates from him, then that part grows and a person like that original is produced from it. If that is so, then a man's offspring is a part of him and a portion of him. Thus His saying ﴿and they have assigned to Him a portion of His servants﴾ — the meaning of *jaʿalū* ("they assigned") is "they judged, asserted and affirmed," and the meaning is that they asserted for Him a portion, and that portion is a servant from among His servants.

Know that if He had said, "And they have assigned from Him a portion to His servants," this would convey that they asserted that a part of His parts had come into being in some of His servants, and that is the child. Likewise His saying ﴿and they have assigned to Him a portion of His servants﴾ means: they asserted for Him a portion, and that portion is a servant from among His servants. The summary is that they asserted a child for Allah. They mentioned other aspects in explaining this view, saying: the *juzʾ* is the female in the language of the Arabs, and they argued for establishing this usage with two verses.

The first is his saying:

*If a free woman happens to be a portion one day, there is no wonder,*
*for the free woman who is kept sometimes becomes a portion.*

And his saying:

*I married her to one of the daughters of al-Aws, one who is a portion,*
*for the pliant ʿawsaj (a tree) within its tents is a gazelle.*

Al-Zajjaj, al-Azhari and the author of *al-Kashshaf* claimed that this usage is corrupt and that these verses are fabricated.

The second view on the interpretation of the verse is that the intended meaning of His saying ﴿and they have assigned to Him a portion of His servants﴾ is the affirmation of partners for Allah. This is because when they affirmed partners for Allah, the Exalted, they claimed that not all the servants belong to Allah, but some belong to Allah and some belong to other than Allah. So they did not assign to Him all His servants, but assigned to Him from them a part and a portion. They said: What indicates that this view is preferable to the first is that if we interpret this verse as a denial of a partner for Allah, and interpret the verse that follows it as a denial of a child for Allah, the verses together encompass the refutation of all the falsifiers.

\* \* \*

**Then He, exalted is He, said:** ﴿Has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen sons for you?﴾

Know that He, exalted is He, arranged this debate in the best of ways. He showed that affirming a child for Allah is impossible, and that, even supposing a child were established, making it a daughter is also impossible. As for the proof that affirming a child for Allah is impossible: a child must be a part of the parent, and whatever has a part is composite, and every composite is contingent. Moreover, whatever is like this accepts joining and separating, union and disunion, and whatever is like this is a created servant, and so cannot be an eternal, pre-eternal god.

As for the second position, namely that supposing a child is established, it is impossible for it to be a daughter: this is because the son is more excellent than the daughter. So if we said that He took daughters for Himself and gave sons to His servants, it would follow that the state of the servant would be more perfect and excellent than the state of Allah. This is refuted by the immediate judgment of reason. It is said: *aṣfaytu fulānan bi-kadhā* — meaning I preferred so-and-so with such-and-such, a preference that results for him in purity, without anyone sharing in it. It is like His saying ﴿Has your Lord preferred you with sons?﴾ [al-Isra': 40].

Then He explained the deficiency of daughters in several respects:

**The first:** His saying ﴿And when one of them is given good tidings of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful, his face becomes dark and he suppresses grief.﴾ The meaning is: how can a sensible person permit affirming for Allah, the Exalted, that whose state is so deficient to this extent? It is reported of one of the Arabs that his wife gave birth to a female, so he abandoned the house in which the woman was. She said:

*What is wrong with Abu Hamzah that he does not come to us?*
*He stays in the house nearest to us.*
*Is he angry that we do not bear sons?*
*We have no say in our affairs, and we take what is given to us.*

His saying *ẓalla* means "became," as most defective verbs are used. The author of *al-Kashshaf* said: it has been read *musawaddun* (مُسْوَدٌّ) and *miswaddun* (مِسْوادٌّ). The estimate is: *wa-huwa musawaddun*, so this clause occupies the position of the predicate.

**The second:** His saying ﴿Is one who is brought up in ornaments, and who is unclear in disputation, [to be ascribed to Him]?﴾

There are issues in it:

**The first issue:** Ḥamzah, al-Kisa'i and Ḥafṣ on the authority of ʿĀṣim read *yunashsha'u* (يُنَشَّأُ) with a *ḍamma* on the *yāʾ*, a *fatḥa* on the *nūn* and a shadda on the *shīn*, in the passive voice, meaning "is raised." The rest read *yunshaʾu* (يُنْشَأُ) with a *ḍamma* on the *yāʾ*, a sukun on the *nūn* and a *fatḥa* on the *shīn*. The author of *al-Kashshaf* said: it has also been read *yunāshaʾu* (يُناشَأُ). He said: the parallel of *munāshaʾah* in the sense of *inshāʾ* is *mughālāh* in the sense of *ighlāʾ*.

**The second issue:** The intended meaning of His saying ﴿Is one who is brought up in ornaments﴾ is to draw attention to her deficiency, namely that one who is raised in ornaments is deficient in essence, because if there were no deficiency in her essence she would not need to adorn herself with ornaments. Then He explained the deficiency of her state by another way, namely His saying ﴿and who is unclear in disputation﴾. He means that when she needs to dispute and contend, she is incapable and is not clear. This is due to the weakness of her tongue, the paucity of her intellect and the dullness of her nature. It is said: rarely does a woman speak when she wants to speak with her proof, except that she speaks with what becomes a proof against her. These aspects indicate her complete deficiency. How, then, is it permissible to attribute them to Him as children!

**The third issue:** The verse indicates that adornment is permitted for women and forbidden for men, because He made that among the defects and causes of deficiency. A man's engaging in it is casting himself into humiliation, and that is forbidden, due to His, peace be upon him, saying: "It is not for a believer to humiliate himself." The adornment of a man is only patience in obedience to Allah and adorning oneself with the adornment of piety. Al-Shafiʿi said:

*One day I donned contentment as a fortress,*
*by which I protect my honour, and I made it a treasure.*
*I did not fear the treacherous age,*
*for its utmost is to strike me with death and poverty.*
*So I prepared for death the God and His pardon,*
*and I prepared for poverty endurance and patience.*

\* \* \*

**Then He, exalted is He, said:** ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, into females.﴾ There are issues in it:

**The first issue:** By His saying "they made," the meaning is "they judged with it." Then He said: ﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾ This is a question in the form of denial, meaning that they did not witness their creation. This is something for which there is no path to knowledge by rational proofs. As for transmitted proofs, all of them are based on establishing prophethood, and these disbelievers deny prophethood, so there is no path for them to establish this claim by transmitted proofs. Thus it is established that they made this claim without knowing it, neither by necessity nor by evidence. Then He threatened them, saying: ﴿Their testimony will be recorded and they will be questioned.﴾ This indicates that speaking without evidence is reprehensible, and that imitation (*taqlid*) entails great blame and severe punishment. The people of verification said: these disbelievers disbelieved in this statement in three respects:

First: affirming a child for Allah, the Exalted.

Second: that this child is a daughter.

Third: the judgment that the angels are female.

**The second issue:** Nafiʿ, Ibn Kathir and Ibn ʿĀmir read *ʿinda al-Raḥmān* (عِنْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ) with a *nūn*. This is the choice of Abu Hatim, who argued for it with several points:

First: it agrees with His saying ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord﴾ [al-A'raf: 206] and His saying ﴿and whoever is with Him﴾ [al-Anbiya': 19].

Second: all creation are His servants, so there is no praise for them in this.

Third: the sense is that the angels are with the Most Merciful, not with these disbelievers, so how did they know that they are females?

As for the rest, they read *ʿibād* (عِبادُ) as the plural of *ʿabd*. It was also said it is the plural of *ʿābid*, like *qāʾim* and *qiyām*, *ṣāʾim* and *ṣiyām*, *nāʾim* and *niyām*. This is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbas and the choice of Abu ʿUbayd, who said: because He, exalted is He, refuted their claim that they are daughters of Allah, and informed that they are servants. This reading is confirmed by His saying ﴿Rather, they are honoured servants﴾ [al-Anbiya': 26].

**The third issue:** Nafiʿ alone read *āʾ-ushhidū* (آأُشْهِدُوا) with a *hamza*, then a long vowel followed by a light soft vowel, and a *ḍamma*, meaning: were they made to witness their creation? And on the authority of Nafiʿ it is also read without the long vowel, in the passive voice. The rest read *ashahidū* (أشَهِدُوا) with a *fatḥa* on the *alif*, from *shahidū*, meaning "they were present."

**The fourth issue:** Whoever argues for the preference of the angels over humans uses this verse, saying: As for the reading *ʿinda* with a *nūn*, this nearness is undoubtedly the nearness of excellence and closeness to Allah, the Exalted, by means of obedience. The word *hum* (هم) necessitates restriction, and the meaning is that they are the ones described by this nearness and no others. Therefore it is necessary that they be more excellent than others, in observance of the word that indicates restriction. As for whoever reads *ʿibād*, the plural of *ʿabd*, we have mentioned that the word *ʿibād* in the Qur'an is specific to the believers. **Then He, exalted is He, said:** ﴿Has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen sons for you?﴾

As for the proof that affirming a child for Allah is impossible: a child must be a part of the parent, and whatever has a part is composite, and every composite is contingent. *What is wrong with Abu Hamzah that he does not come to us?*
*He stays in the house nearest to us.*
*Is he angry that we do not bear sons?*
*We have no say in our affairs, and we take what is given to us.*

The rest read *yunshaʾu* (يُنْشَأُ) with a *ḍamma* on the *yāʾ*, a sukun on the *nūn* and a *fatḥa* on the *shīn*. The author of *al-Kashshaf* said: it has also been read *yunāshaʾu* (يُناشَأُ). He said: the parallel of *munāshaʾah* in the sense of *inshāʾ* is *mughālāh* in the sense of *ighlāʾ*.

*One day I donned contentment as a fortress,*
*by which I protect my honour, and I made it a treasure.*
*I did not fear the treacherous age,*
*for its utmost is to strike me with death and poverty.*
*So I prepared for death the God and His pardon,*
*and I prepared for poverty endurance and patience.*

This is because when they affirmed partners for Allah, the Exalted, they claimed that not all the servants belong to Allah, but some belong to Allah and some belong to other than Allah. So they did not assign to Him all His servants, but assigned to Him from them a part and a portion. They said: What indicates that this view is preferable to the first is that if we interpret this verse as a denial of a partner for Allah, and interpret the verse that follows it as a denial of a child for Allah, the verses together encompass the refutation of all the falsifiers.

\* \* \*

**Then He, exalted is He, said:** ﴿Has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen sons for you?﴾

Know that He, exalted is He, arranged this debate in the best of ways. He showed that affirming a child for Allah is impossible, and that, even supposing a child were established, making it a daughter is also impossible. As for the proof that affirming a child for Allah is impossible: a child must be a part of the parent, and whatever has a part is composite, and every composite is contingent. Moreover, whatever is like this accepts joining and separating, union and disunion, and whatever is like this is a created servant, and so cannot be an eternal, pre-eternal god.

As for the second position, namely that supposing a child is established, it is impossible for it to be a daughter: this is because the son is more excellent than the daughter. So if we said that He took daughters for Himself and gave sons to His servants, it would follow that the state of the servant would be more perfect and excellent than the state of Allah. This is refuted by the immediate judgment of reason. It is said: *aṣfaytu fulānan bi-kadhā* — meaning I preferred so-and-so with such-and-such, a preference that results for him in purity, without anyone sharing in it. It is like His saying ﴿Has your Lord preferred you with sons?﴾ [al-Isra': 40].

Then He explained the deficiency of daughters in several respects:

**The first:** His saying ﴿And when one of them is given good tidings of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful, his face becomes dark and he suppresses grief.﴾ The meaning is: how can a sensible person permit affirming for Allah, the Exalted, that whose state is so deficient to this extent? It is reported of one of the Arabs that his wife gave birth to a female, so he abandoned the house in which the woman was. She said:

*What is wrong with Abu Hamzah that he does not come to us?*
*He stays in the house nearest to us.*
*Is he angry that we do not bear sons?*
*We have no say in our affairs, and we take what is given to us.*

His saying *ẓalla* means "became," as most defective verbs are used. The author of *al-Kashshaf* said: it has been read *musawaddun* (مُسْوَدٌّ) and *miswaddun* (مِسْوادٌّ). The estimate is: *wa-huwa musawaddun*, so this clause occupies the position of the predicate.

**The second:** His saying ﴿Is one who is brought up in ornaments, and who is unclear in disputation, [to be ascribed to Him]?﴾

The rest read *yunshaʾu* (يُنْشَأُ) with a *ḍamma* on the *yāʾ*, a sukun on the *nūn* and a *fatḥa* on the *shīn*. The author of *al-Kashshaf* said: it has also been read *yunāshaʾu* (يُناشَأُ). He said: the parallel of *munāshaʾah* in the sense of *inshāʾ* is *mughālāh* in the sense of *ighlāʾ*.

Then He explained the deficiency of her state by another way, namely His saying ﴿and who is unclear in disputation﴾. He means that when she needs to dispute and contend, she is incapable and is not clear. This is due to the weakness of her tongue, the paucity of her intellect and the dullness of her nature. It is said: rarely does a woman speak when she wants to speak with her proof, except that she speaks with what becomes a proof against her. These aspects indicate her complete deficiency. How, then, is it permissible to attribute them to Him as children!

A man's engaging in it is casting himself into humiliation, and that is forbidden, due to His, peace be upon him, saying: "It is not for a believer to humiliate himself." The adornment of a man is only patience in obedience to Allah and adorning oneself with the adornment of piety. Al-Shafiʿi said:

*One day I donned contentment as a fortress,*
*by which I protect my honour, and I made it a treasure.*
*I did not fear the treacherous age,*
*for its utmost is to strike me with death and poverty.*
*So I prepared for death the God and His pardon,*
*and I prepared for poverty endurance and patience.*

**Then He, exalted is He, said:** ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, into females.﴾ There are issues in it:

**The first issue:** By His saying "they made," the meaning is "they judged with it." Then He said: ﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾ This is a question in the form of denial, meaning that they did not witness their creation. This is something for which there is no path to knowledge by rational proofs. As for transmitted proofs, all of them are based on establishing prophethood, and these disbelievers deny prophethood, so there is no path for them to establish this claim by transmitted proofs. Thus it is established that they made this claim without knowing it, neither by necessity nor by evidence. Then He threatened them, saying: ﴿Their testimony will be recorded and they will be questioned.﴾ This indicates that speaking without evidence is reprehensible, and that imitation (*taqlid*) entails great blame and severe punishment. The people of verification said: these disbelievers disbelieved in this statement in three respects:

First: affirming a child for Allah, the Exalted.

Second: that this child is a daughter.

Third: the judgment that the angels are female.

**The second issue:** Nafiʿ, Ibn Kathir and Ibn ʿĀmir read *ʿinda al-Raḥmān* (عِنْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ) with a *nūn*. This is the choice of Abu Hatim, who argued for it with several points:

First: it agrees with His saying ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord﴾ [al-A'raf: 206] and His saying ﴿and whoever is with Him﴾ [al-Anbiya': 19].

Second: all creation are His servants, so there is no praise for them in this.

Third: the sense is that the angels are with the Most Merciful, not with these disbelievers, so how did they know that they are females?

As for the rest, they read *ʿibād* (عِبادُ) as the plural of *ʿabd*. It was also said it is the plural of *ʿābid*, like *qāʾim* and *qiyām*, *ṣāʾim* and *ṣiyām*, *nāʾim* and *niyām*. This is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbas and the choice of Abu ʿUbayd, who said: because He, exalted is He, refuted their claim that they are daughters of Allah, and informed that they are servants. This reading is confirmed by His saying ﴿Rather, they are honoured servants﴾ [al-Anbiya': 26].

**The third issue:** Nafiʿ alone read *āʾ-ushhidū* (آأُشْهِدُوا) with a *hamza*, then a long vowel followed by a light soft vowel, and a *ḍamma*, meaning: were they made to witness their creation? And on the authority of Nafiʿ it is also read without the long vowel, in the passive voice. The rest read *ashahidū* (أشَهِدُوا) with a *fatḥa* on the *alif*, from *shahidū*, meaning "they were present."

**The fourth issue:** Whoever argues for the preference of the angels over humans uses this verse, saying: As for the reading *ʿinda* with a *nūn*, this nearness is undoubtedly the nearness of excellence and closeness to Allah, the Exalted, by means of obedience. The word *hum* (هم) necessitates restriction, and the meaning is that they are the ones described by this nearness and no others. Therefore it is necessary that they be more excellent than others, in observance of the word that indicates restriction. As for whoever reads *ʿibād*, the plural of *ʿabd*, we have mentioned that the word *ʿibād* in the Qur'an is specific to the believers. So His saying ﴿they are servants of the Most Merciful﴾ conveys the restriction of servanthood to them. When the word that indicates servanthood indicates excellence and honour, the word that indicates the restriction of servanthood indicates the restriction of excellence, merit and honour to them, and that necessitates that they are more excellent than others. And Allah knows best.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 43, verses 15–19:**

**His saying, may He be exalted:** ﴿And they have assigned to Him a portion of His servants. The purpose of this is to draw attention to the feebleness of their intellects and the foolishness of their minds. In the verse there are issues:

**The first issue:** ʿĀṣim, in the transmission of Abū Bakr, read *juzʾun* (جُزْءٌ) with a *ḍamma* on the *zāy* and the *hamza* throughout the Qur'an. Both are dialectal variants. As for Ḥamzah, when he pauses on it he says *juzan* (جُزًا) with a *fatḥa* on the *zāy* and without a *hamza*.

﴿And they say, "Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them." They have no knowledge of that; they merely guess.﴾ ﴿Have We given them a Book before this, so that they hold fast to it?﴾ ﴿Rather, they say, "We found our fathers following a community, and we are guided by their footsteps."﴾ ﴿And so We did not send before you a warner to any town but its affluent ones said, "We found our fathers following a community, and we follow in their footsteps."﴾ ﴿He said, "Even if I brought you better guidance than what you found your fathers upon?" They said, "We disbelieve in that with which you have been sent."﴾ ﴿So We took vengeance upon them. Then see how was the end of the deniers.﴾

Know that He, the Exalted, has related another kind of their disbelief and their doubts, which is that they said: "Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them." On this there are several issues.

The first issue: The Mu'tazilah said: This verse indicates the invalidity of the view of the Mujbirah (the compulsionists) that the disbelief of the disbeliever occurs by the will of God, from two aspects:

The first: He, the Exalted, related from them that they said, "Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them," and this is the explicit statement of the Mujbirah. Then He, the Exalted, refuted it with His saying, "They have no knowledge of that; they merely guess." Thus it is established that He related the doctrine of the Mujbirah and then followed it with refutation and invalidation, so it is established that this doctrine is false. A parallel to this is His saying in Surat al-An'am: "The idolaters will say, 'Had God willed, we would not have associated anything with Him'" [al-An'am: 148], up to His saying: "Say, 'Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? You follow only assumption, and you are only guessing.'" [al-An'am: 148]

The second aspect: He, the Exalted, related from them, before this verse, the kinds of their disbelief:

The first of them is His saying: "And they have made for Him from His servants a portion" [al-Zukhruf: 15].

The second is His saying: "And they have made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females" [al-Zukhruf: 19].

The third is His saying, Exalted is He: "And they say, 'Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them.'" So when He related these three statements, one after another, and it is established that the first two are pure disbelief, then this third statement must likewise be disbelief. Know that al-Wahidi, in *al-Basit*, answered this from two aspects:

The first is what al-Zajjaj mentioned: that His saying, "They have no knowledge of that," refers to their statement "the angels are females" and to their statement "the angels are daughters of God."

The second: that by their saying, "Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them," they meant that He had commanded us to do this, that He was pleased with it, and that He approved it for us. So He rejected this from them. This is what al-Wahidi mentioned in response. In my view, these two aspects are weak. As for the first: He, the Exalted, related from the people two false statements and explained the reason for their falsity, then after them related a third doctrine on a matter foreign to the first two issues, then passed judgment of falsity and threat upon it. Thus He directed this refutation away from what He mentioned immediately after it, toward an earlier, utterly unrelated statement.

As for the second aspect: it is also weak, because His saying, "Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them," contains no clarification connected to that will, and leaving things unspecified contradicts the evidence. Therefore the meaning must be: "Had God willed that we not worship them, we would not have worshipped them." The word "law" (*law*, "had") indicates the non-existence of one thing because of the non-existence of another. This indicates that God's will was not present for their non-worship, and this is exactly the doctrine of the Mujbirah. So the refutation and invalidation return to this meaning. Some people answered this argument by saying that they only spoke these words in mockery and derision, and for this reason they deserved censure and blame. Sahib *al-Kashshaf* answered this from two aspects:

The first: there is nothing in the wording that indicates they spoke mockingly, and asserting what has no evidence is invalid.

The second: He, the Exalted, related three things from them: that they "made for Him from His servants a portion" [al-Zukhruf: 15], that they made the angels females, and that they said, "Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them." If we say that the censure came for the third statement because they uttered it in earnest, then the situation regarding the first two statements must be the same. It would follow that if they had spoken those things in earnest they would have been right, and it is known that this is disbelief. As for the claim that the censure of the first two statements was directed at the statements themselves, whereas for the third it was not directed at the statement itself but at presenting it in mockery, this would cause the disruption of the composition, and that is not permissible in the speech of God.

Know that the true answer in my view to this objection is what we mentioned in Surat al-An'am: that these people only said this statement because they used God's will for disbelief as proof that the command to believe could not be sent. They believed that the command and the will must necessarily correspond. In our view this is false. So these people did not deserve blame merely for their saying that God wills disbelief from the disbeliever, but because they said: since He willed disbelief from the disbeliever, it must be ugly of Him to command the disbeliever to believe. When we direct the blame and censure to this point, the Mu'tazilah's argument from this verse falls. The full explanation is mentioned in Surat al-An'am. And God knows best.

The second issue: When He, the Exalted, related that false doctrine from them, He said: "They have no knowledge of that; they merely guess." The explanation is: it is as if it were said that the people say: since God willed disbelief from the disbeliever and created in him that which necessitates that disbelief, it must be ugly of Him to command him to believe, because such a obligation is ugly among us, and therefore it is ugly regarding the absent (God). So He, the Exalted, said: "They have no knowledge of that," meaning: they have no knowledge of the soundness of this analogy (*qiyas*, reasoning by analogy). That is because the actions and rulings of one of us are based on considering benefits and harms, since everything other than God benefits from the attainment of benefits and is harmed by the occurrence of harms. Therefore, the natural disposition and intellect of such a being inevitably compel it to build its rulings and actions upon the consideration of benefits. As for God, the Glorified and Exalted, nothing benefits Him and nothing harms Him. How, then, can one be certain that He, the Exalted, builds His rulings and actions upon the consideration of benefits, given this great difference that is evident? So His saying, "They have no knowledge of that," means: they have no knowledge of the soundness of analogizing the Absent upon the Present in this matter.
* * *
Then He said: "They merely guess." The second: that by their saying, "Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them," they meant that He had commanded us to do this, that He was pleased with it, and that He approved it for us. \* \* \*

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Rather, I gave enjoyment to these and their fathers﴾, meaning the people of Makkah, who are the descendants of Abraham, by extending their lifespan and blessings. So they were deceived by the respite and busied themselves with luxury, the pursuit of desires, and obedience to Satan, away from the word of monotheism. ﴿Until there came to them the truth﴾, which is the Qur'an, ﴿and a clear messenger﴾, who made the message clear and explicit by the signs and clear proofs he brought. Yet they denied him, called him a sorcerer, and said that what he brought was magic, and they disbelieved in him.

The connection of the discourse (*wajh al-naẓm*) is that, since they relied on the imitation of their fathers and did not reflect on the proof, they were deceived by the prolonged respite and by Allah's granting them the enjoyment of this world's bounties, so they turned away from the truth.

The author of *al-Kashshaf* (al-Zamakhshari) said: If it is asked, what is the reading of one who reads ﴿mattaʿtu﴾ (مَتَّعْتُ) with a fatha on the *tā'*? His purpose in this speech is to rebuke the wrongdoer, not to disparage his own action.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Rather, I gave enjoyment to these and their fathers﴾, meaning the people of Makkah, who are the descendants of Abraham, by extending their lifespan and blessings. So they were deceived by the respite and busied themselves with luxury, the pursuit of desires, and obedience to Satan, away from the word of monotheism. ﴿Until there came to them the truth﴾, which is the Qur'an, ﴿and a clear messenger﴾, who made the message clear and explicit by the signs and clear proofs he brought. Yet they denied him, called him a sorcerer, and said that what he brought was magic, and they disbelieved in him.

The connection of the discourse (*wajh al-naẓm*) is that, since they relied on the imitation of their fathers and did not reflect on the proof, they were deceived by the prolonged respite and by Allah's granting them the enjoyment of this world's bounties, so they turned away from the truth.

The author of *al-Kashshaf* (al-Zamakhshari) said: If it is asked, what is the reading of one who reads ﴿mattaʿtu﴾ (مَتَّعْتُ) with a fatha on the *tā'*? We say: It is as if Allah, glorified is He, was objecting to Himself in His saying ﴿and he made it a word lasting among his descendants that they might return﴾, so He said: "Rather, I gave them enjoyment with what I gave them enjoyment with, namely the length of life and the abundance of provision, until that busied them away from the word of monotheism." He intended by this the emphasis in reproaching them, because when He grants them enjoyment through increased blessings, it becomes obligatory for them to make that a cause for increased gratitude and steadfastness in monotheism, not to associate partners with Him and set up rivals to Him. Its example is that a man complains of the harm done to him by one who has done him good, and then turns to himself and says: "You are the cause of that, by your kindness and your good done to him." His purpose in this speech is to rebuke the wrongdoer, not to disparage his own action.

Al-Razi, *Mafatih al-Ghayb* (*The Keys to the Unseen*), commentary on verses 26 to 30 of Surah al-Zukhruf (43):

Allah's words: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free of what you worship,"﴾ ﴿except He who created me, for He will guide me.﴾ ﴿And he made it a word lasting among his descendants that they might return.﴾ ﴿Rather, I gave enjoyment to these and their fathers until there came to them the truth and a clear messenger.﴾ ﴿And when there came to them the truth, they said, "This is magic, and indeed we are disbelievers in it."﴾

Know that when Allah, exalted is He, explained in the preceding verse that those disbelievers had no caller calling them to those false statements except the blind imitation (*taqlid*) of their fathers and forebears, and then explained that this is a false path and a corrupt method, and that returning to proof is better than relying on blind imitation, He followed it with this verse. Its purpose is to mention another aspect that proves the invalidity of the doctrine of blind imitation. Its demonstration is in two ways:

The first: Allah related about Abraham, peace be upon him, that he disassociated himself from the religion of his fathers on the basis of proof. We say: Either blind imitation of fathers in religious matters is forbidden or it is permitted. If it is forbidden, then the doctrine of blind imitation is refuted. If it is permitted, then it is known that the most honourable of the fathers of the Arabs is Abraham, peace be upon him, because they have no pride or honour except that they are among his descendants. Given this, imitating this father, who is the most honourable of fathers, is more fitting than imitating all other fathers. Once it is established that imitating him is more fitting than imitating others, we say: He abandoned the religion of the fathers and ruled that following proof is better than following the fathers. Given this, it is obligatory to imitate him in abandoning the imitation of the fathers, and it is obligatory to imitate him in preferring proof over imitation. Once this is established, we say: It has become clear that the claim that imitation is obligatory entails the prohibition of imitation. And whatever its establishment leads to its negation is invalid. So it is necessary that the doctrine of imitation be invalid. This is a subtle path to refuting imitation, and it is what this verse intends.

The second: In explaining that abandoning imitation and returning to following proof is better both in this world and in religion, Allah explained that when Abraham, peace be upon him, turned away from the way of his father to following proof, Allah, for that reason, made his religion and his creed lasting among his descendants until the Day of Resurrection. As for the religions of his fathers, they were effaced and nullified. Thus it is established that returning to following proof remains praiseworthy in its effect until the Hour is established, while blind imitation and obstinacy have effects that are cut off, and nothing of them remains in this world, neither report nor trace. From these two aspects it is established that following proof and abandoning imitation is better. This is the explanation of the primary purpose of this verse. Let us now return to the explanation of the words of the verse.

As for His words ﴿Indeed, I am free of what you worship﴾: al-Kisa'i, al-Farra', al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjaj said: ﴿barā'un﴾ (بَراءٌ) is a verbal noun (*masdar*) that is not made dual or plural, like ʿadl (عَدْلٌ) and riḍā (رِضاً). The Arabs say: "I am free (al-barā') of you and clear (al-khalā') of you," and "We are free (al-barā') of you and clear (al-khalā')," and they do not say "al-barāʾān" or "al-barāʾūn," because the meaning is "those who possess disassociation" and "those who possess disassociation." But if you say barī' (بَرِيءٌ) and khaliyy (خَلِيٌّ), you make them dual and plural.

Then He excepted His Creator from the disassociation, saying: ﴿except He who created me﴾. The meaning is: I disassociate myself from what you worship, except from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. **His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man of the two towns?"﴾**

﴿Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others by degrees, so that some may take others in service. But the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.﴾

Know that this is the fourth kind of their disbelief which Allah the Exalted related about them in this surah. These wretched people said: The office of Allah's messengership is a noble office, so it befits only a noble man. They were right in that, but they added to it a corrupt premise, namely that the noble man is the one who has abundant wealth and status, and Muhammad is not like that, so Allah's messengership does not befit him. This office befits only a man of great status and abundant wealth in one of the two towns, namely Makkah and al-Ta'if. The exegetes (mufassirun) said: The one in Makkah is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and the one in al-Ta'if is Urwa ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi. Then Allah the Exalted refuted this doubt in two ways.

The first is His saying: ﴿Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord?﴾ The explanation of this answer has several aspects:

The first: We have caused the disparity in the worldly positions, and none of the creation has been able to change it. So the disparity that We have caused in the positions of religion and prophethood, by their not being able to dispose of it, is more fitting.

The second: The meaning may be that the singling out of that wealthy man with that abundant wealth was only because of Our judgment, Our bounty and Our kindness toward him. How then is it reasonable by intellect that We should make Our kindness to him in abundance of wealth a proof against Us that We should also show kindness to him by prophethood?

The third: Since We caused the disparity in the bestowal of worldly positions without a prior cause, why is it not permissible that We likewise cause disparity in the bestowal of positions of religion and prophethood, without a prior cause? This is the explanation of the answer. Now we return to the explanation of the words. We say: the hamza in His saying ﴿أهم يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَةَ رَبِّكَ﴾ (ʾa-hum yaqsimūna raḥmata rabbik) is for denial, indicating ignorance, astonishment at their aversion and their arbitrariness, and that they would be the ones who manage the matter of prophethood. Then He gave an example for this, saying: ﴿We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others by degrees﴾. And in this there are issues:

The first issue: We have caused this disparity among the servants in strength and weakness, knowledge and ignorance, cleverness and dullness, fame and obscurity. We did this only because, if We made them equal in all these states, no one would serve anyone, and none of them would become subjected to another. Then that would lead to the ruin of the world and the corruption of the order of the worldly life. Furthermore, none of the creation has been able to change Our judgment or to depart from Our decree. If they are unable to turn away from Our judgment in the matters of this world despite its scantiness and lowliness, how can they then object to Our judgment and decree in singling out servants with the office of prophethood and messengership?

The second issue: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world﴾ requires that all the kinds of their livelihoods come about only by the judgment of Allah and His determination. This requires that lawful and unlawful provision alike are all from Allah the Exalted.

The second aspect of the answer: What is meant by His saying ﴿But the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate﴾? Its explanation is that when Allah the Exalted singles out some of His servants with a kind of His grace and mercy in religion, this mercy is better than the wealth which they amass, because the world is on the verge of ending and perishing, whereas the grace and mercy of Allah endure forever and ever.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had it not been that mankind would become one community, We would have given to those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver for their houses, and staircases of silver on which they could ascend,﴾ ﴿and doors for their houses, and couches on which they could recline,﴾ ﴿and ornaments of gold. And all of that is nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life. But the Hereafter, with your Lord, is for the God-fearing.﴾ ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he becomes his companion.﴾ ﴿Indeed, they (the devils) bar them from the way, while they think that they are guided.﴾ ﴿Until, when he comes to Us, he says: "Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! Wretched is the companion!"﴾ ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you wronged, that you are sharing in the punishment.﴾

In the verse there are several issues:

First issue: Allah, exalted is He, answered the doubt they raised, which was based on preferring the rich over the poor, with a third point. He showed that the benefits and pleasures of this world are base and worthless in the sight of Allah, and He demonstrated their worthlessness through His saying: ﴿And had it not been that mankind would become one community﴾. The meaning is: Had it not been that people would be drawn to disbelief when they see the disbeliever in abundance of goodness and provision, I would have given them the most of the means that bring about luxury:

The first: that their roofs be of silver.

The second: staircases also of silver, on which they ascend.

The third: that We make for their houses doors of silver, and couches also of silver, on which they recline.

Then He said: ﴿and ornaments of gold (zukhrufan)﴾. It has two interpretations:

One of them: it means gold.

The second: it means adornment, as evidenced by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿until, when the earth takes on its adornment (zukhrufaha) and becomes beautified﴾ [Yunus: 24]. So according to the first interpretation, the meaning is: We would also give them much gold along with that. According to the second: We would give them great adornment at every door. Then Allah, exalted is He, showed that all of that is the enjoyment of the worldly life. He only called it "enjoyment" because a person benefits from it for a little while, and then it ends immediately. As for the Hereafter, it is lasting and everlasting, and it is with Allah, exalted is He, and in His judgment, for the God-fearing, those who are free of love of this world and who turn toward love of the Master. The summary of the answer is that those ignorant people thought that the wealthy man was more deserving of the station of messengerhood than Muhammad because of his poverty. So Allah, exalted is He, showed that wealth and status are worthless in the sight of Allah, and that they are on the verge of disappearing. Therefore, obtaining them does not confer honor. And Allah knows best.

Second issue: Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read "sathfan" (سَقْفًا) with a fatha on the sin and a sukun on the qaf, in the singular form, intending the category, as in His saying: ﴿So the roof fell upon them from above them﴾ [al-Nahl: 26]. The rest read "suqufan" (سُقُفًا) in the plural. They differed: it is said that it is the plural of "saqf," like "rahn" and "ruhun." Abu 'Ubayd said: "There is no third reading for them." It was also said: "suquf" is the plural of "suquf," like "ruhun" and "ruhun," and "zubur" and "zubur," so it is the plural of the plural.

Third issue: His saying: ﴿for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful, for their houses﴾. Here "li-buyutihim" (لِبُيُوتِهِمْ) is a badal al-ishtimal (inclusive apposition, a substitute that includes the referent) for "li-man yakfuru" (لِمَن يَكْفُرُ). The author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari) said: "It is read as 'ma'arij' (مَعارِجَ) and 'ma'arij' (مَعارِيجَ). 'Ma'arij' is the plural of 'ma'raj,' or a collective noun for 'mi'raj,' and these are the ascents to the high dwellings, like stairs and ladders." "Alayha yazhharun" means: on those staircases they ascend. As for the accusative in His saying "wa-zukhrufan" (وَزُخْرُفًا), there are two views: it is said that the meaning is "We would make for their houses roofs of silver, and We would make for them adornment," and it is said: "of silver and of adornment." When the preposition is omitted, the noun becomes accusative.

As for His saying: ﴿and all of that is nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life (wa-in kullu dhalika lamma mata'u al-hayat al-dunya)﴾, 'Asim and Hamzah read "lamma" (لَمّا) with a doubled mim, and the rest read it with a single mim. As for Hamzah's reading with the doubling, he took "lamma" to mean "illa" (إلّا, except). Sibawayh reported: "I beseech you by Allah, lamma you did (لَما فَعَلْتَ)," meaning: "except that you did." This reading is strengthened by the fact that in the codex of Ubayy it reads: "wa-ma dhalika illa mata'u al-hayat al-dunya" ("and that is only the enjoyment of the worldly life"), which shows that "lamma" means "illa." As for the reading with a single mim, al-Wahidi said: the word "ma" is superfluous, and the construction is "lamata'u al-hayat al-dunya." Abu al-Hasan said: "The correct form is the single mim, because 'lamma' in the sense of 'illa' is not known." It is related from al-Kisa'i that he said: "I do not know the rationale for the doubling."

Fourth issue: The Mu'tazilah (the rationalist theological school) said: The verse indicates that Allah, exalted is He, only withheld the blessings of this world from people because if He had done that to them, it would have led them to disbelief. Therefore, He did not do that to them in order that it not lead them to disbelief. This indicates several rulings:

The first: if He did not do to them what would lead them to disbelief, then it is even more fitting that He would not create disbelief in them.

The second: it is established that performing lutf (divine benevolence that facilitates faith, a term the Mu'tazilah use for this concept) stands in place of removing the excuse and the cause. So when Allah, exalted is He, stated that He did not do that in order to remove excuse and cause from them, this indicates that He must do for them everything that is a lutf calling them to faith. Thus this verse, from this angle, indicates that it is obligatory upon Allah, exalted is He, to perform lutf.

The third: it is established by this verse that Allah, exalted is He, only does what He does and refrains from what He refrains from for the sake of wisdom and benefit, and this indicates that the rulings and acts of Allah, exalted is He, are grounded in benefits and causes.

If it is said: When Allah, exalted is He, stated that if He had opened the doors of blessings to the disbeliever, that would have been a cause for people to gather in disbelief, why did He not do that for the Muslims, so that it would become a cause for people to gather in Islam? We say: Because under this assumption, people would gather in Islam seeking worldly gain, and this faith would be the faith of hypocrites. So it was more fitting to restrict matters for the Muslims, so that everyone who enters Islam enters it out of following the evidence and seeking the pleasure of Allah, exalted is He. In that case, his reward is greatly magnified for this reason.

* * *

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he becomes his companion.﴾ The purpose of this is to warn about the afflictions of this world. That is because whoever is successful in wealth and status becomes like one who is blinded (al-a'sha) to the remembrance of Allah. Whoever becomes like that becomes one of the companions of the misguided, misguiding devils. This is the connection of this statement to what precedes it. The author of al-Kashshaf said: "It is read as 'wa-man ya'shu' (وَمَن يَعْشُ) with a damma and with a fatha on the shin. The difference between them is that when a defect occurs in one's sight, it is said 'ʿashiya' (عَشِيَ). When one looks like someone with weak sight, though there is no defect in him, it is said 'ʿashā' (عَشى). A parallel is 'ʿaraja' (عَرِجَ) for one who has the defect, and 'ʿarija' (عَرَجَ) for one who walks with the gait of a lame man without being lame." Al-Hutay'ah said: "Whenever you come to him, you squint (ta'shu) toward the light of his fire," meaning you look at it with the gaze of one whose sight is weak, because of the great size of the fuel and the breadth of the light. It is also read as "ya'shu" (يَعْشُو), with "man" as a relative pronoun that does not carry the meaning of a condition. The reader of this form should read "nuqayyidu" as nominative. The meaning of the reading with a fatha is: "whoever becomes blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful," which is the Qur'an, based on His saying: ﴿deaf, dumb, blind﴾. As for the reading with a damma, its meaning is: "whoever feigns blindness to His remembrance," that is, he knows that it is the truth, but he pretends ignorance and feigns blindness, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them﴾ [al-Naml: 14]. And ﴿We appoint for him a devil﴾: Muqatil said: "We attach to him a devil." ﴿So he becomes his companion﴾.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, they (the devils) bar them from the way﴾, meaning: the devils bar them from the path of guidance and truth. He mentioned the reference to the human and the devils with a plural pronoun, because His saying ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil﴾ implies plurality, even though the wording is singular. ﴿While they think that they are guided﴾, meaning: the devils bar the disbelievers from the way, and the disbelievers think that they are guided. Then He returned to the singular, saying: ﴿Until, when he comes to Us﴾, meaning the disbeliever. It is also read as "jaʼana" (جاءانا) (dual), meaning the disbeliever and his devil. It is related: when the disbeliever is raised from his grave on the Day of Resurrection, his devil takes him by the hand and does not leave him until Allah makes them both go to the Fire. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had it not been that mankind would become one community, We would have given to those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver for their houses, and staircases of silver on which they could ascend,﴾ ﴿and doors for their houses, and couches on which they could recline,﴾ ﴿and ornaments of gold. Whoever becomes like that becomes one of the companions of the misguided, misguiding devils. This is the connection of this statement to what precedes it. The author of al-Kashshaf said: "It is read as 'wa-man ya'shu' (وَمَن يَعْشُ) with a damma and with a fatha on the shin. The difference between them is that when a defect occurs in one's sight, it is said 'ʿashiya' (عَشِيَ). When one looks like someone with weak sight, though there is no defect in him, it is said 'ʿashā' (عَشى). A parallel is 'ʿaraja' (عَرِجَ) for one who has the defect, and 'ʿarija' (عَرَجَ) for one who walks with the gait of a lame man without being lame." Al-Hutay'ah said: "Whenever you come to him, you squint (ta'shu) toward the light of his fire," meaning you look at it with the gaze of one whose sight is weak, because of the great size of the fuel and the breadth of the light. It is also read as "ya'shu" (يَعْشُو), with "man" as a relative pronoun that does not carry the meaning of a condition. The reader of this form should read "nuqayyidu" as nominative. The meaning of the reading with a fatha is: "whoever becomes blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful," which is the Qur'an, based on His saying: ﴿deaf, dumb, blind﴾. As for the reading with a damma, its meaning is: "whoever feigns blindness to His remembrance," that is, he knows that it is the truth, but he pretends ignorance and feigns blindness, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them﴾ [al-Naml: 14]. And ﴿We appoint for him a devil﴾: Muqatil said: "We attach to him a devil." ﴿So he becomes his companion﴾.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, they (the devils) bar them from the way﴾, meaning: the devils bar them from the path of guidance and truth. He mentioned the reference to the human and the devils with a plural pronoun, because His saying ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil﴾ implies plurality, even though the wording is singular. ﴿While they think that they are guided﴾, meaning: the devils bar the disbelievers from the way, and the disbelievers think that they are guided. Then He returned to the singular, saying: ﴿Until, when he comes to Us﴾, meaning the disbeliever. It is also read as "jaʼana" (جاءانا) (dual), meaning the disbeliever and his devil. It is related: when the disbeliever is raised from his grave on the Day of Resurrection, his devil takes him by the hand and does not leave him until Allah makes them both go to the Fire. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿he says: "Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts!"﴾ The intended meaning: "Would that there had come to be between me and you a distance of the greatest extent!"

They differed in interpreting His saying ﴿the distance of the two easts﴾, and they gave several views:

The first: Most of them said: the intended meaning is the distance between the east and the west. It is a habit of the Arabs to name two opposites by the name of one of them. Al-Farazdaq said: "Ours are its two moons and the rising stars," meaning the sun and the moon. They say for Kufa and Basra: "the two Basras (al-Basratan)"; for the morning and afternoon: "the two afternoons (al-'asrān)"; for Abu Bakr and Umar: "the two Umars (al-'Umarān)"; for water and dates: "the two blacks (al-aswadān)."

The second: The astronomers say: the movement from the east to the west is the movement of the greatest sphere, and the movement from the west to the east is the movement of the fixed stars, and the movements of the represented orbits of the planets other than the moon. If that is so, then east and west are each an east in relation to something else. Thus it is established that applying the term "east" to each of the two directions is literal.

The third: They said: this is to be understood as the east of summer and the east of winter, and there is a great distance between them. This, in my view, is far-fetched, because the purpose of His saying ﴿he says: "Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts!"﴾ is to emphasize the extent of the distance, and this emphasis arises only when mentioning a distance beyond which no greater distance is possible. The distance between the summer east and the winter east is not like that, so it is far-fetched to read the expression that way.

The fourth: The senses indicate that the daily movement occurs by the rising of the sun from the east to the west. As for the moon, it appears at the beginning of the month on the western side, then continues to advance toward the eastern side. This indicates that the east of the moon's movement is the west. If that is established, then the side called "east" is the east of the sun, but it is the west of the moon; and the side called "west" is the east of the moon, but it is the west of the sun. In this reckoning, it is correct to call east and west "the two easts." Perhaps this view is closest to conforming to the wording and to preserving the intended meaning among all the views. And Allah knows best.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Wretched is the companion!﴾, meaning: the disbeliever says to that devil: ﴿"Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! Wretched is the companion!"﴾, referring to you. This is what pertains to the explanation of the words. The purpose of this discourse is to belittle this world and to show the great harms that lie in wealth and status. That is because abundance of wealth and status makes a person like one blinded to contemplating the remembrance of Allah, exalted is He. Whoever becomes like that becomes a companion of the devil. Whoever becomes like that strays from the path of guidance and truth and remains a companion of the devil in this world and in the Hereafter. Being in the company of the devil is a state that entails severe harm on the Day of Resurrection, to the extent that the disbeliever says: ﴿"Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! Wretched is the companion!"﴾, referring to you. Thus it is established by what we have mentioned that abundance of wealth and status brings about complete deficiency and deprivation in religion and in this world. And when this becomes clear, it becomes clear that those who said ﴿"Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from one of the two towns?"﴾ spoke a corrupt statement and a false doubt.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you wronged, that you are sharing in the punishment.﴾ His saying "annakum" (أنَّكم) is in the nominative position as the subject. The meaning: "Your sharing in the punishment will not benefit you today." The reason for this is that people say: "When a calamity becomes general, it becomes easier to bear." Al-Khansa' expressed this meaning:

"Were it not for the abundance of those weeping around me over their brothers, I would have killed myself.
But they do not weep like my brother, yet I console my soul about him with consolation."

Thus Allah, exalted is He, showed that sharing in that punishment does not bring alleviation, as it did in the world. The reasons for this are several:

The first: that punishment is severe, and each one's preoccupation with himself distracts him from the state of the other; therefore, sharing in the punishment does not bring lightening.

The second: when a group shares in punishment, each one helps his companion with what he is able to do, and some lightening results from this; but this meaning is impossible on the Day of Resurrection.

The third: sitting with one's companion brings many kinds of consolation.

So God, exalted is He, made clear that although the devil is a companion, sitting with him on the Day of Resurrection does not entail consolation or lightening of the punishment. In the Kitab of Ibn Mujahid, from Ibn 'Amir, it is reported that he recited ﴿إذ ظلمتم إنكم﴾ with a kasra on the alif (إنكم), while the rest of the readers recited ﴿أنكم﴾ with a fatha on the alif. And God knows best.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had it not been that mankind would become one community, We would have given to those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver for their houses, and staircases of silver on which they could ascend,﴾ ﴿and doors for their houses, and couches on which they could recline,﴾ ﴿and ornaments of gold. And all of that is nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life. But the Hereafter, with your Lord, is for the God-fearing.﴾ ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he becomes his companion.﴾ ﴿Indeed, they (the devils) bar them from the way, while they think that they are guided.﴾ ﴿Until, when he comes to Us, he says: "Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! Wretched is the companion!"﴾ ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you wronged, that you are sharing in the punishment.﴾

In the verse there are several issues:

First issue: Allah, exalted is He, answered the doubt they raised, which was based on preferring the rich over the poor, with a third point. He showed that the benefits and pleasures of this world are base and worthless in the sight of Allah, and He demonstrated their worthlessness through His saying: ﴿And had it not been that mankind would become one community﴾. The meaning is: Had it not been that people would be drawn to disbelief when they see the disbeliever in abundance of goodness and provision, I would have given them the most of the means that bring about luxury:

The first: that their roofs be of silver.

The second: staircases also of silver, on which they ascend.

The third: that We make for their houses doors of silver, and couches also of silver, on which they recline.

Then He said: ﴿and ornaments of gold (zukhrufan)﴾. It has two interpretations:

One of them: it means gold.

The second: it means adornment, as evidenced by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿until, when the earth takes on its adornment (zukhrufaha) and becomes beautified﴾ [Yunus: 24]. So according to the first interpretation, the meaning is: We would also give them much gold along with that. According to the second: We would give them great adornment at every door. Then Allah, exalted is He, showed that all of that is the enjoyment of the worldly life. He only called it "enjoyment" because a person benefits from it for a little while, and then it ends immediately. As for the Hereafter, it is lasting and everlasting, and it is with Allah, exalted is He, and in His judgment, for the God-fearing, those who are free of love of this world and who turn toward love of the Master. The summary of the answer is that those ignorant people thought that the wealthy man was more deserving of the station of messengerhood than Muhammad because of his poverty. So Allah, exalted is He, showed that wealth and status are worthless in the sight of Allah, and that they are on the verge of disappearing. Therefore, obtaining them does not confer honor. And Allah knows best.

Second issue: Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read "sathfan" (سَقْفًا) with a fatha on the sin and a sukun on the qaf, in the singular form, intending the category, as in His saying: ﴿So the roof fell upon them from above them﴾ [al-Nahl: 26]. The rest read "suqufan" (سُقُفًا) in the plural. They differed: it is said that it is the plural of "saqf," like "rahn" and "ruhun." Abu 'Ubayd said: "There is no third reading for them." It was also said: "suquf" is the plural of "suquf," like "ruhun" and "ruhun," and "zubur" and "zubur," so it is the plural of the plural.

Third issue: His saying: ﴿for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful, for their houses﴾. Here "li-buyutihim" (لِبُيُوتِهِمْ) is a badal al-ishtimal (inclusive apposition, a substitute that includes the referent) for "li-man yakfuru" (لِمَن يَكْفُرُ). The author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari) said: "It is read as 'ma'arij' (مَعارِجَ) and 'ma'arij' (مَعارِيجَ). 'Ma'arij' is the plural of 'ma'raj,' or a collective noun for 'mi'raj,' and these are the ascents to the high dwellings, like stairs and ladders." "Alayha yazhharun" means: on those staircases they ascend. As for the accusative in His saying "wa-zukhrufan" (وَزُخْرُفًا), there are two views: it is said that the meaning is "We would make for their houses roofs of silver, and We would make for them adornment," and it is said: "of silver and of adornment." When the preposition is omitted, the noun becomes accusative.

As for His saying: ﴿and all of that is nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life (wa-in kullu dhalika lamma mata'u al-hayat al-dunya)﴾, 'Asim and Hamzah read "lamma" (لَمّا) with a doubled mim, and the rest read it with a single mim. As for Hamzah's reading with the doubling, he took "lamma" to mean "illa" (إلّا, except). Sibawayh reported: "I beseech you by Allah, lamma you did (لَما فَعَلْتَ)," meaning: "except that you did." This reading is strengthened by the fact that in the codex of Ubayy it reads: "wa-ma dhalika illa mata'u al-hayat al-dunya" ("and that is only the enjoyment of the worldly life"), which shows that "lamma" means "illa." As for the reading with a single mim, al-Wahidi said: the word "ma" is superfluous, and the construction is "lamata'u al-hayat al-dunya." Abu al-Hasan said: "The correct form is the single mim, because 'lamma' in the sense of 'illa' is not known." It is related from al-Kisa'i that he said: "I do not know the rationale for the doubling."

Fourth issue: The Mu'tazilah (the rationalist theological school) said: The verse indicates that Allah, exalted is He, only withheld the blessings of this world from people because if He had done that to them, it would have led them to disbelief. Therefore, He did not do that to them in order that it not lead them to disbelief. This indicates several rulings:

The first: if He did not do to them what would lead them to disbelief, then it is even more fitting that He would not create disbelief in them.

The second: it is established that performing lutf (divine benevolence that facilitates faith, a term the Mu'tazilah use for this concept) stands in place of removing the excuse and the cause. So when Allah, exalted is He, stated that He did not do that in order to remove excuse and cause from them, this indicates that He must do for them everything that is a lutf calling them to faith. Thus this verse, from this angle, indicates that it is obligatory upon Allah, exalted is He, to perform lutf.

The third: it is established by this verse that Allah, exalted is He, only does what He does and refrains from what He refrains from for the sake of wisdom and benefit, and this indicates that the rulings and acts of Allah, exalted is He, are grounded in benefits and causes.

If it is said: When Allah, exalted is He, stated that if He had opened the doors of blessings to the disbeliever, that would have been a cause for people to gather in disbelief, why did He not do that for the Muslims, so that it would become a cause for people to gather in Islam? We say: Because under this assumption, people would gather in Islam seeking worldly gain, and this faith would be the faith of hypocrites. So it was more fitting to restrict matters for the Muslims, so that everyone who enters Islam enters it out of following the evidence and seeking the pleasure of Allah, exalted is He. In that case, his reward is greatly magnified for this reason.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, they (the devils) bar them from the way﴾, meaning: the devils bar them from the path of guidance and truth. Then He returned to the singular, saying: ﴿Until, when he comes to Us﴾, meaning the disbeliever. It is also read as "jaʼana" (جاءانا) (dual), meaning the disbeliever and his devil. It is related: when the disbeliever is raised from his grave on the Day of Resurrection, his devil takes him by the hand and does not leave him until Allah makes them both go to the Fire. "Were it not for the abundance of those weeping around me over their brothers, I would have killed myself.

The first: that punishment is severe, and each one's preoccupation with himself distracts him from the state of the other; therefore, sharing in the punishment does not bring lightening.
